advisory.finding: For a genuinely-new Jira Blocks link (surfaced by Jira on BOTH endpoints) where neither local ticket yet owns the edge, both per-ticket inbound passes emit an add — X gets `blocks`->Y and Y gets `depends_on`->X — because the counterpart-owns-inverse guard only suppresses once one side already stores the edge. This double-adds a single edge in the fresh-adoption path, the same mirror duplication the dedup is meant to avoid.
scenarios: A human adds a Blocks link directly in Jira between two active, synced tickets that had no local dep; one reconcile pass emits an add on each endpoint for the one edge.

advisory.finding: The outbound REMOVE-path direction mapping (outbound_links._diff_link_removals) is NOT pinned by the captured live-ground-truth test, despite both source docstrings claiming it is. test_link_direction_absolute.py exercises only inbound_differ._diff_links_inbound; the REMOVE path's direction is asserted only against author-authored synthetic fixtures in test_link_removal_sync.py. Since the change explicitly warns that a hand-authored fixture encoding the wrong convention is the chronic anti-oracle that let prior inversions ship, the REMOVE-side mapping can silently re-invert and drift from the ADD side while the ground-truth test stays green.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive `this_id` with the same `local_ticket.get("ticket_id", local_ticket.get("id"))` fallback the caller uses to key `local_tickets_by_id`.
evidence: run_differs.py:556: `    local_by_id = {t.get("ticket_id", t.get("id", "")): t for t in local_tickets}`
run_differs.py:429/431 also use `t.get("ticket_id", t.get("id", ""))` — the module's established id-derivation contract that the new code does not follow
dropped.finding: The cross-ticket inverse-aware dedup uses `this_id = local_ticket.get("ticket_id")`, but the caller (`run_differs.py`) builds `local_tickets_by_id` and derives ids everywhere with the fallback `t.get("ticket_id", t.get("id", ""))`. If a local ticket carries only `id` (no `ticket_id`), `this_id` is None, so the guard `(inverse, this_id) in _deps_as_set(counterpart)` can never match and the spurious mirror-add is emitted anyway — defeating the dedup for those tickets.
scenarios: A local ticket serialized with `id` but no `ticket_id` participates in a blocking edge; the counterpart owns the inverse edge; the mirror-add is re-emitted every pass instead of being deduped.
